chapter_title: Paul at Ephesus, Part 1: The Apostle's Life, Letters, and Ephesian Years
learning_objective: The learner will classify twelve places by the journey on which the Book of Acts first brings Paul there (first, second, or third journey, or the voyage to Rome), correctly placing at least 10 of 12.

**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify twelve places by the journey on which the Book of Acts first brings Paul there (first, second, or third journey, or the voyage to Rome), correctly placing at least 10 of 12. **Prerequisites:** Paul's missionary journeys, the Book of Acts as the source for them, Roman roads and the sailing season, and the province of Asia (all defined in the chapter above this block); our cruise route (Chapter 2, "The Trip Itinerary"). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 12 places, the learner chooses one of four journey labels before the journey routes are revealed. A choice is correct when it matches the "Correct journey" column in Content. Mastery is 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt. Turning route layers on and off and reading place infoboxes are exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Paul's main stay in Ephesus was his first visit there; in fact Acts brings him there briefly at the end of the second journey. (2) Paul visited Crete on a missionary journey; Acts brings him there only as a prisoner, on the voyage to Rome. (3) Athens was a center of Paul's work; Acts gives it a short visit on the second journey. (4) Paul visited every port on our cruise; he never went to Byzantium, and Acts never brings him to Heraklion or Delphi. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying places by journey makes the learner connect each city to a stage of Paul's life, an Understand task. Committing a choice before the routes appear turns the map from a picture into a prediction the learner can check, and the misconception items are chosen so that a reader who has only skimmed will predict wrongly and learn from the correction. **Content:** Map extent: the Mediterranean from Rome (west) to Damascus and Jerusalem (east), and from Philippi (north) to Jerusalem (south). Routes, each drawn as a line through its waypoints in this order (coordinates are latitude, longitude): 1. First journey (c. 46–48 CE; Acts 13–14): Antioch in Syria (36.20, 36.16) → Seleucia Pieria (36.12, 35.93) → Salamis (35.18, 33.90) → Paphos (34.76, 32.41) → Perga (36.96, 30.85) → Pisidian Antioch (38.31, 31.19) → Iconium (37.87, 32.48) → Lystra (37.58, 32.45) → Derbe (37.35, 33.36) → Lystra → Iconium → Pisidian Antioch → Perga → Attalia (36.88, 30.70) → Antioch in Syria. 2. Second journey (c. 49–52 CE; Acts 15:36–18:22): Antioch in Syria → Tarsus (36.92, 34.89) → Derbe → Lystra → Iconium → Troas (39.75, 26.16) → Neapolis (40.94, 24.41) → Philippi (41.01, 24.29) → Thessalonica (40.64, 22.94) → Berea (40.52, 22.20) → Athens (37.97, 23.73) → Corinth (37.91, 22.88) → Ephesus (37.94, 27.34) → Caesarea (32.50, 34.89) → Antioch in Syria. (Acts says "through Syria and Cilicia," the region of Tarsus, without naming the city; the line passes through Tarsus as the main city of Cilicia.) 3. Third journey (c. 52–57 CE; Acts 18:23–21:17): Antioch in Syria → Iconium → Pisidian Antioch → Ephesus (Acts names only "the region of Galatia and Phrygia" before Ephesus; the line passes through Iconium and Pisidian Antioch as the main cities of that region) → Troas → Philippi → Thessalonica → Corinth → Philippi → Troas → Assos (39.49, 26.34) → Mitylene (39.10, 26.55) → Chios (38.37, 26.14) → Samos (37.69, 26.94) → Miletus (37.53, 27.28) → Cos (36.89, 27.29) → Rhodes (36.44, 28.22) → Patara (36.26, 29.32) → Tyre (33.27, 35.20) → Ptolemais (32.92, 35.08) → Caesarea → Jerusalem (31.78, 35.23). 4. Voyage to Rome (c. 59–60 CE; Acts 27:1–28:16): Caesarea → Sidon (33.56, 35.37) → Myra (36.26, 29.98) → Cnidus (36.69, 27.37) → Fair Havens, Crete (34.93, 24.81) → Malta, St. Paul's Bay (35.95, 14.40) → Syracuse (37.07, 15.29) → Rhegium (38.11, 15.65) → Puteoli (40.82, 14.12) → Rome (41.90, 12.50). 5. Our cruise and land route, November 11–23, 2026 (shown as a separate layer): Istanbul (41.01, 28.98) → Çanakkale (40.15, 26.41) → Kuşadası (37.86, 27.26) → Rhodes (36.44, 28.22) → Heraklion (35.34, 25.13) → Piraeus (37.94, 23.64) → Athens (37.97, 23.73) → Delphi (38.48, 22.50) → Athens. Also shown as unconnected markers with infoboxes: Tarsus ("Paul's birthplace, according to Acts"), Damascus (33.51, 36.29; "Paul's call, about 33–36 CE"), Jerusalem ("Where Paul was arrested, about 57 CE"). The 12 places to classify, in this fixed order: | # | Place | Correct journey | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Paphos, Cyprus | First | Paul and Barnabas crossed Cyprus to Paphos at the start of the first journey (Acts 13:6). | | 2 | Iconium | First | Paul and Barnabas preached in Iconium's synagogue on the first journey (Acts 14:1). | | 3 | Lystra | First | Paul was stoned and left for dead at Lystra on the first journey (Acts 14:19); he returned on the second, when Timothy joined him. | | 4 | Troas | Second | At Troas, Paul saw the vision of the man of Macedonia (Acts 16:8–9). | | 5 | Philippi | Second | Lydia became the first convert in Europe at Philippi (Acts 16:12–15). | | 6 | Athens | Second | Paul's only visit to Athens, a short one, came on the second journey (Acts 17:15–34). | | 7 | Corinth | Second | Paul stayed eighteen months in Corinth on the second journey (Acts 18:11). | | 8 | Ephesus | Second | Acts first brings Paul to Ephesus briefly at the end of the second journey (Acts 18:19–21); his long stay came on the third. | | 9 | Miletus | Third | Paul said farewell to the Ephesian elders at Miletus near the end of the third journey (Acts 20:17). | | 10 | Rhodes | Third | Paul's ship stopped at Rhodes on the way to Jerusalem (Acts 21:1). | | 11 | Fair Havens, Crete | Voyage to Rome | Paul reached Crete only as a prisoner, on the voyage to Rome (Acts 27:8). | | 12 | Malta | Voyage to Rome | Paul's ship was wrecked on Malta (Acts 28:1). | Answer counts: First 3, Second 5, Third 2, Voyage to Rome 2. **Provenance:** Routes and the 12 answers come from the Book of Acts, chapters and verses as cited, and from the chapter sections "Paul's Missionary Journeys" and "The Farewell at Miletus." Journey dates are the approximate reconstructions in the chapter's journeys table. Coordinates are approximate positions of the ancient sites (or the modern town for Iconium, Antioch in Syria, Rhodes, and our ports), rounded to 0.01°; before building, check each against the coordinates in its Wikipedia article and correct any that differ by more than 0.05°. Our route comes from Chapter 2's itinerary table. The sim labels the journey routes "Routes as told in Acts; dates approximate." **Rules:** - A place's correct answer is the journey on which Acts first brings Paul there, not the journey on which he stayed longest. - Before the learner answers, only the 12 places, our route layer, and the three unconnected markers are visible; journey routes are hidden. - After all 12 places are answered, all four journey routes appear and can be toggled one at a time or all together. - Places that appear on more than one route (Lystra, Troas, Philippi, Ephesus, Corinth) show every journey that passes through them in their infobox after the reveal, with the first one marked "first visit." - A place is "on our route" when it is one of our stops in Content item 5; after the reveal, the sim lists the places Paul and our trip share: Athens, Rhodes, and the region of Ephesus (Kuşadası). **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the map with our route and the 12 unanswered places, and reads the question. 2. For each place, in order, the learner chooses First, Second, Third, or Voyage to Rome. The place is marked answered and the feedback for that place appears. 3. After the twelfth answer, the four journey routes appear, and the score is shown. 4. The learner toggles each journey on and off and opens the infoboxes for places visited more than once. 5. The learner should notice that the second journey reached the most places, that Ephesus appears on two journeys, and that Paul reached Crete only as a prisoner. **Feedback:** Twelve items, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [Why]." Incorrect: "Not quite. [Why]" followed, for item 8, by "Watch for the difference between a first visit and a long stay," and for item 11, by "Crete appears in Acts only on the voyage to Rome." After the twelfth item the sim shows "You placed [n] of 12. Mastery is 10." and, if n < 10, offers "Try again," which clears all answers and hides the routes. **Starting State:** Our route from Istanbul to Athens and Delphi is drawn; the 12 places are marked but unanswered; the question reads "On which journey did Acts first bring Paul to each of these places?" **Chapter Anchors:** Journeys dated about 46–48, 49–52, and 52–57 CE, and the voyage about 59–60 CE; Paul stayed eighteen months in Corinth; Ephesus visited briefly on the second journey and for two to three years on the third; Paul's ship ran along the south coast of Crete before the wreck on Malta; Lydia of Thyatira the first convert in Europe; 12 places.
